Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: A businesswoman sets up a charity to provide toys for young children of low income families. Which term most accurately describes these toys?

options.A: free goods
options.B: merit goods
options.D: public goods

questions.questionText: What will happen to an industry’s supply curve if new firms enter the industry?

options.A: It will shift to the left at any given price.
options.B: It will shift to the right at any given price.
options.C: There will be a downward movement along the supply curve.
options.D: There will be an upward movement along the supply curve.

questions.questionText: D D shows an individual’s initial demand curve for public transport.
Two goods X and Y have a positive cross-elasticity of demand and upward-sloping supply curves. What will be the effect of a reduction in the price of good Y?

options.A: The demand for good X will increase.
options.B: The demand for good Y will decrease.
options.C: The price of good X will decrease.
options.D: The quantity of good X supplied will increase.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes the meaning of price elasticity of supply?

options.A: how much price changes when there has been a change in supply
options.B: how much supply changes when there is a change in demand
options.C: how much supply changes when there is a change in price
options.D: how much supply changes when there is a change in the price of a substitute

options.B: W and Z only
options.D: Z only

questions.questionText: Goods X and Y are complements and have upward-sloping supply curves. What will be the effect on the equilibrium price and quantity of good X of an increase in the supply of good Y? quantity of X price of X

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: What is generally considered to be one of the advantages of using the price mechanism as a rationing device?

options.A: It ensures that goods are allocated in accordance with the wants of consumers.
options.B: It ensures that suppliers cannot make excessive profits.
options.C: No one can be prevented from consuming a good if they are willing and able to pay the market price.
options.D: The allocation of goods is determined by consumers’ wealth.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a competitive market in equilibrium with price P and quantity Q sold. V S price P W U D O Q quantity Which area represents the producer surplus?

options.A: OPWQ minus OUWQ
options.B: OPWQ minus UPW
options.D: OVWQ minus PVW

questions.questionText: The government fixes a maximum price for wheat flour below the market equilibrium price. After the maximum price is imposed, which statement is not correct?

options.A: Producers’ revenue is increased.
options.B: Some consumers may encourage illegal sales.
options.C: The quantity supplied of flour will decrease.
options.D: There will be an excess demand for flour.

In 2014 Egypt reduced subsidies on fossil fuels such as gasoline and diesel. The diagram shows the initial equilibrium at point X. What will be the new equilibrium after the reduction of subsidies? S price 1

options.B: C X A D D O quantity

questions.questionText: What is an aim of a transfer payment?

options.A: It allows the government to alter the final distribution of income.
options.B: It provides a ceiling for levels of income across the economy.
options.C: It removes the need for state subsidies.
options.D: It rewards the activity of a factor of production.

questions.questionText: There have been recent calls for the UK government to nationalise its railways. What would not be a reason for nationalising the railways?

options.A: Private rail companies often charge high ticket prices.
options.B: Private rail companies may exploit monopoly power.
options.C: Railways are an essential part of national infrastructure.
options.D: Railways should be treated as a public good.

options.A: Money national output decreased by 10%.

questions.questionText: Between June and the end of July 2016 the UK pound sterling depreciated by 11% against a basket of currencies of the UK’s major trading partners. The diagram shows the original aggregate demand curve AD and the original aggregate supply curve AS for the UK economy before June 2016. The equilibrium is at X. What will be the new equilibrium for the UK economy as a result of the depreciation of the pound sterling? price AS level 1 A

options.B: X D C AD O real output

questions.questionText: Which item is not included in the current account of a country’s balance of payments?

options.A: exports of services
options.B: interest on foreign loans
options.D: the purchase of foreign assets

questions.questionText: A government wishes to raise the value of the external exchange rate of its currency. What should it do?

options.A: discourage inward foreign direct investment
options.B: raise interest rates
options.C: raise the level of aggregate demand in the economy
options.D: remove quotas on imported products

questions.questionText: Country X conducts 60% of its trade with country Y and 40% of its trade with country Z. The initial value of the trade-weighted exchange rate index of country X is 100. What will be its new trade-weighted exchange rate index value if its currency falls in value by 20% against the currency of country Y and rises by 10% against the currency of country Z?
The index for a country’s terms of trade changed from 100 in year 2015, to 104 in year 2016. What could have caused this change?

options.A: a fall in export prices with import prices unchanged
options.B: a fall in revenue from the export of services
options.C: an appreciation of the country’s currency
options.D: a rise in the value of imports

options.A: an import quota to restrict the supply of goods
options.B: a rise in interest rates to encourage the supply of savings
options.C: a specific tax on the supply of goods to raise revenue
options.D: a subsidy to businesses to promote the supply of training courses
